completion: This works, but `users.filter(u => u.active)` says the same thing in one line and nobody has to trace the loop to see what it does. Also `== true` is redundant — `u.active` is already a boolean. Small thing, but it's the kind of line that slows a reviewer down for no reason. Nice and simple logic otherwise, good instinct to keep it readable.

If `db.find(id)` doesn't find anything, this throws on `user.name` with a confusing error instead of telling you the user wasn't found. Add a check and throw (or return) something explicit when `user` is missing — future-you debugging this at 1am will thank you. The happy path is clean, that's the right instinct.

Two things worth fixing: `JSON.parse` can throw on malformed input, and you're assuming `data.items` exists without checking. Wrap the parse in a try/catch or check `response.ok` first, and guard `data.items` with a default. Everything after that point reads fine — you're just trusting the network a little too much.

This saves one at a time when they're independent — `Promise.all(items.map(save))` would run them concurrently and be noticeably faster once the list grows. Not a bug, just leaving speed on the table. Keep the sequential version if `save` has to run in order for some reason, but if not, batch it.

Nothing wrong here, just formatting: add spaces around operators and after commas so this is as easy to skim as the logic is simple. Consistent style is what lets a reviewer trust the diff without reading every character. Good, small, single-purpose functions — that part's exactly right.
